lens: Compliance review — data classification, audit-chain emission, secret handling, RLS/tenant-scoping, regulatory pack coverage, auditability (who/when/what/why)
answer: The four sub-checks (check_rust_default_language, check_naming_convention, check_scorecard_render, check_consensus_debate_evidence) are pure local-filesystem scanners that read workspace-owned JSON and filename strings. They do not touch, transmit, store, or derive any regulated data class (no PHI, PCI, PII, PIPA, CHILDREN, or TENANT_SCOPED content enters or exits the functions). Accordingly, no RLS boundary is crossed and no regulatory pack update is triggered. However, two compliance-relevant gaps are present: (1) the four functions mutate observable CI state (SubCheckResult returned to the composite report, which is emitted to stdout/evidence on every run) but emit no audit-chain event — ADR-0069 requires emission for any state change surfaced to evidence; the task_group_completion event at timestamp 1778812400 in audit-chain.jsonl records TG2 as a whole but contains no per-sub-check emission, which means a compliance team cannot answer 'which sub-check produced which finding on which run' from the audit trail alone. (2) The check_consensus_debate_evidence function reads the content of every JSON file under evidence/multispectrum and evidence/per-change; while today those files contain only structural metadata, the scan pattern is open-ended — if a future evidence file ever contains a regulated-data excerpt (e.g., a PHI-tagged incident report embedded in evidence), these functions will silently read and discard it with no data-class gate. No secrets are handled. No raw secrets appear in the code, findings strings, or evidence files reviewed. SecretReference is not applicable. Auditability of the functions themselves is partial: who/when is captured at task-group granularity, but what/why at sub-check granularity is missing from the audit chain.
key_claims: Data class touched is 'none' for all four sub-checks: inputs are filesystem paths and JSON structural metadata; no regulated attributes (PHI, PCI, PII, PIPA, CHILDREN, TENANT_SCOPED) are read, stored, or emitted.

ADR-0069 audit-chain emission is required for state changes surfaced to evidence. The composite report produced by these sub-checks is written to evidence/per-change on every CI run (per the render_report_json + task_group_completion pattern observed in audit-chain.jsonl). No per-sub-check emission event exists in the audit-chain; the 1778812400 task_group_completion event names the four sub-checks collectively but records no finding-level 'who/when/what/why'.

The audit-chain.jsonl entry at timestamp 1778812400 records cargo_test pass and new_sub_checks array but does not record: (a) which sub-check produced which finding on the emission run, (b) the findings[] strings, (c) the SubCheckStatus values, or (d) the session that triggered the check. A compliance team auditing 'why was rust-default-language NotYetArmed on 2026-05-14' cannot reconstruct the answer from the chain alone.

Secret handling: not applicable. No credential, API key, token, or secret reference appears in any of the four function bodies, their findings strings, or the evidence files examined (synthesis, F7 review, audit-chain tail).

RLS / tenant-scoping: not applicable. All four functions scan global workspace-level directories (scripts/, specs/cross-cutting/, registries/cross-cutting/, evidence/, templates/). No tenant-scoped path segments exist; WorkspaceContext.workspace_root is workspace-global. No RLS boundary is touched or bypassed.

Regulatory pack impact: none currently. The code is language/tooling policy enforcement (P14/P15) and evidence-structure validation. No KR, EU, or US regulatory pack requirement is implicated by the content scanned today.

Forward-looking data-class risk: check_scorecard_render and check_consensus_debate_evidence call read_to_string on all .json files under evidence/multispectrum and evidence/per-change without a data-class gate. If a future evidence file is tagged with a regulated data class (PHI, PCI, TENANT_SCOPED), these functions will silently read it. No data-class label check or access-control gate exists at the read site.

Auditability verdict: PARTIAL. Task-group-level 'who/when' is in the chain (session_id, timestamp_unix, change_id). Sub-check-level 'what' (findings[]) and 'why' (SubCheckStatus reason) are not emitted to the chain.
uncertainty_areas: Whether ADR-0069 scope covers internal CI lane state changes (SubCheckResult) or only user-visible data mutations. If ADR-0069 applies only to user-data state, the missing sub-check emission may be out of scope. The audit-chain.jsonl pattern observed (ip_status_flip, adr_accepted, durable_migration_slice_complete) suggests it covers structural/process state changes, but the ADR text was not directly read in this session.

Whether a future evidence file could legitimately contain regulated content. Current evidence files reviewed (multispectrum, per-change) contain only structural metadata. The risk is latent, not present.

Whether the composite report JSON (render_report_json output) is written to a durable evidence path on every run or only on explicit invocation. If it is always persisted, the missing per-sub-check audit emission is a day-1 gap. If it is ephemeral (stdout only), the compliance bar may be lower.
